name: kube-hunter - Kubernetes Vulnerability Scanner
description: kube-hunter probes a Kubernetes cluster for security weaknesses: exposed API server, insecure kubelet (read-only 10255 and authed 10250), etcd, dashboard, and known CVEs. It maps the attack surface from an external, internal-network, or in-pod vantage point and reports hunters/vulnerabilities with severity.
notes:
=== INSTALL / RUN ===
  pip install kube-hunter       # or docker run --rm aquasec/kube-hunter

=== REMOTE SCAN (external) ===
  kube-hunter --remote <ip>
  kube-hunter --cidr <cidr>          # sweep a range

=== INTERNAL NETWORK SCAN ===
  kube-hunter --interface           # scan all local interfaces/subnets

=== IN-POD (active, from a compromised pod) ===
  kube-hunter --pod                 # uses the pod service account + looks at kubelet/API
  kube-hunter --pod --active        # include exploit-level checks (intrusive)

=== KEY FINDINGS TO CHASE ===
  - Kubelet 10250 (authed) / 10255 (read-only) exposed -> list pods, exec
  - API server anonymous access / insecure port 8080
  - etcd 2379 open -> dump all secrets
  - Dashboard without auth

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  peirates          # interactive k8s attack/escalation
  kubeletctl        # kubelet API abuse
  kubectl           # if a kubeconfig/token is found
  nmap -p 6443,10250,10255,2379,8080

examples.label: Remote scan of an API endpoint

recommended.note: Manual kube enumeration once the surface is mapped.
Reference of Kubernetes ports to interpret results.

defense.why_it_works: Kubernetes components historically expose network services (kubelet, etcd, API insecure port, dashboard) that may lack authentication when misconfigured. kube-hunter enumerates these and matches known CVE patterns.
defense.prerequisites: Network reachability to cluster components, or execution inside a pod with a mounted service-account token.
defense.impact: Full inventory of exploitable cluster weaknesses (unauth kubelet exec, open etcd secrets, anonymous API) leading to cluster takeover.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1046] Bursts of connections to 10250/10255/2379/6443/8080 from one source; kubelet access logs showing /pods and /run or /exec from unusual clients; API server audit logs with anonymous or scanning user agents.
defense.artifacts: API server audit logs (user=system:anonymous, userAgent scanning), kubelet request logs, network flow to control-plane ports, NetworkPolicy drops.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=k8s (dest_port=10250 OR dest_port=10255 OR dest_port=2379 OR dest_port=8080)
| stats count dc(dest_port) as ports by src_ip
| where ports > 2
defense.elastic_kql: destination.port:(10250 or 10255 or 2379 or 8080) and network.direction:inbound
defense.sentinel_kql:
let cp_ports = dynamic([10250,10255,2379,8080,6443]);
VMConnection
| where DestinationPort in (cp_ports)
| summarize Ports=dcount(DestinationPort), Count=count() by SourceIp, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where Ports > 2
defense.prevention: Authn/authz on kubelet (disable read-only 10255, require TLS auth on 10250); disable insecure API port; firewall etcd to control plane only; NetworkPolicies restricting pod-to-control-plane; RBAC least privilege; audit logging enabled.

detections.name: Kubernetes control-plane port sweep (kube-hunter)
detections.logic:
let cp_ports = dynamic([10250,10255,2379,8080,6443]);
VMConnection
| where DestinationPort in (cp_ports)
| summarize Ports=dcount(DestinationPort), Count=count() by SourceIp, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where Ports > 2
detections.tuning: Allowlist cluster monitoring sources; alert on external/pod-origin sweeps
